svg.title: How a standing review is recognised, and how the retyped review command picks its lane
svg.desc: Left panel: three lookups decide whether a scoring run already has a review in flight - the reflex's recorded dispatch, a live pointer whose node id is review-of- plus the source node, and, added here, a live review-role pointer whose declared write path names the record the dispatch composes from the reviewed run. Any match suppresses the run's review-missing obligation. Right panel: the composed command chooses its lane through the same candidate ordering the reflex uses - the owning backend leads, the local backend follows, the rest come alphabetically - and a backend the flight configuration excludes from review routing is never named; the local spelling stands in only when no candidate remains.
svg.text: A standing review, and the lane a retyped review names
Recognition is keyed on the record a review was told to write; the printed command selects its lane by the reflex's own ordering.
A - is a review of this run already in flight?
a scoring run: complete, no review stored for its head
1. the reflex's recorded review dispatch,
and its review run still has a live pointer
2. a live pointer whose node id is
review-of- followed by the source node
3. a live review-role pointer whose declared
write path names this run's record
added here: the id is not review-of- plus the source
any one match
in flight: the run is not review-missing
B - which lane does the printed command name?
first: the owning run's recorded backend
the review is of that run; its lane was the owner's choice
then: the locally served backend
named --local, not --backend, when it is chosen
last: the remaining configured backends
in a stable alphabetical order
a backend excluded from review routing is
never named, on any fallback
review_excluded_backends is a rule, not a note
--backend <lane>, or --local when none remains
Both halves read one source of truth: the recognition uses the record path the dispatch composes from
the reviewed run, and the lane uses the candidate ordering the reflex already runs on, so the command
a reader retypes and the command the reflex executes select through the same rule rather than two.
